headline: Purchase of The Landing School building signed; five programs proposed for September 2027.
summary: Money from the Southern Maine Administrative Collaborative's fund balance paid off the building's debt, and the district now owns the building. Five programs for September 2027 were presented for approval, and the DOE was said to have approved funding for them. The district will keep using NWEA for its through-year tests, but the spring science test will use a new Maine assessment. Policy second readings and revisions were also approved, all unanimously.
decisions: Approved nominations and appointments on the consent agenda, unanimously.
Approved second reading of the travel expense reimbursements policy, unanimously.
Approved second reading of the School Facility Fee Schedule, unanimously.
Approved second reading of the policy on students with diagnosed allergies and sensitivities, unanimously.
Approved revisions to the general rules for student participation in athletics and co-curricular activities, unanimously.
Approved revision of the Community Use of School Facilities policy, unanimously.
Approved review of the School Committee Officers policy, unanimously.
Approved review of the executive sessions policy, unanimously.
Approved the executive session law review, unanimously.
Approved School Committee member compensation and expenses policy, unanimously.
Approved revision of the Grants rule, unanimously.
Approved the Comprehensive Health and Safety Emergency Management Plan for 2025, unanimously.
Approved review of the School Records Retention policy, unanimously.
discussion: Landing School programs: Members asked how the five programs for September 2027 were picked, why aquaculture was moved to year two, and how start-up costs would be paid. The programs were chosen from student interest and existing equipment, and DOE funding was said to be approved for them.

Legislative reception update: The York County event drew both parties, and superintendents plan to invite the Education Committee to one of their meetings. Members suggested a joint meeting with the City Council on bills, held in December or January.

State testing change: The new spring science test will be the first use of a new Maine product, and the district will keep NWEA for its other tests. Members said staff are frustrated by another test change and that the training format is not yet known.

Charter review: The charter commission is reviewing the charter one article at a time, with two readings for each change. Members asked whether voters would vote on each change separately, and individual votes were described as the likely approach.
